title: vfife case file, format 1

ArcControlSpec.description:
The displacement an arc is measured on (1.3): one
node's translation, instead of the norm of the whole state. Displacement
control with the load factor as the unknown -- OpenSees' DisplacementControl
integrator -- so the pushed point moves on at every increment and the
path cannot turn back down an unloading branch; it cannot follow a
snap-back of that displacement.
ArcControlSpec.title: ArcControlSpec

ArcLengthSpec.description:
Crisfield's cylindrical arc length: the load factor
becomes an unknown, so the path can pass a limit point -- a pushover's
peak, a snap-through, a snap-back.

initial.title: Initial
initial.description: the first increment's load factor (which sets the arc length)

target_iterations.title: Target Iterations
target_iterations.description: iterations an increment should take: the arc scales by sqrt(desired / taken)

stop.description: where to stop when the load factor does not reach 1

steps.title: Steps
steps.description: the steps that use it, by name; all of them when left out (the others take load-controlled Newton)

control.description: measure the arc on this one displacement (1.3): displacement control with the load factor unknown; the controlled displacement never goes back, and cannot follow its own snap-back; the whole state's norm when left out

ArcLengthSpec.title: ArcLengthSpec

ArcSpec.description: A line drawn as a curve between its two end points (1.1).

rise.title: Rise
rise.description: the rise: how far the curve is from the chord at its middle, along `up` (negative: below)

shape.title: Shape
shape.description: `parabola` (nodes evenly along the chord, the usual arch axis) or `circle` (evenly by angle)

up.title: Up
up.description: the direction of the rise (not along the chord; default global +z)

ArcSpec.title: ArcSpec

ArcStopSpec.description:
Where an arc-length step ends when the load factor never reaches 1:
the mean displacement of a region along a direction reaching `value`.

value.title: Value
value.description: stop when it reaches this displacement (signed)

ArcStopSpec.title: ArcStopSpec

region.title: Region
region.description: exactly one target: a mesh region, or one or more reinforcement sets

reinforcement.title: Reinforcement
reinforcement.description: one or more names in `reinforcement`: the bars this (bar) section describes

orientation.title: Orientation
orientation.description: beam/connector: a vector fixing the section's local y axis (not parallel to the member)

releases.title: Releases
releases.description: beam end releases, from i_rx, i_ry, i_rz, j_rx, j_ry, j_rz (i = first node); a pin at both ends is [i_ry, i_rz, j_ry, j_rz]

end_offsets.title: End Offsets
end_offsets.description: rigid end offsets (1.21): {i: [x, y, z], j: [x, y, z], axes: local|global, per: line|member, axial: elastic|full}, the vectors from the nodes to the ends of the member's elastic part (`local`: the member's axes from its nodes' chord and `orientation`). A rigid end zone is an offset along the member, a section whose centroid is below its nodes one across it. `axial: full` takes a frame beam's axial and torsional stiffness over the length between the nodes; `elastic`, the default, over the elastic part

coordinate_system.title: Coordinate System
coordinate_system.description: connector: `local` (x along the chord, y from `orientation`) or `global` components

bond.title: Bond
bond.description: embedded bars: `{type: bond_ceb | bond_cyclic, ...}` gives the bar its own dofs and a bond-slip law; absent = perfect bond

segment_length.title: Segment Length
segment_length.description: embedded bars: segment length (m) for every line of the set, when the geometry gives none

divisions.title: Divisions
divisions.description: embedded bars: segments per line, when the geometry gives none

transverse_penalty.title: Transverse Penalty
transverse_penalty.description: bonded bars: stiffness holding the bar across its axis (N/m); default the bar's own E A / L_trib. A numerical device, not a dowel

host_deduction.title: Host Deduction
host_deduction.description: subtract the host's E*eps from the bar (elastic hosts only; the solver refuses it with a damaging host -- see elements/truss.py)

anchorage.title: Anchorage
anchorage.description: fiber beams: strain penetration, {region, bar_diameter}; bonded bars: `ends` / `start` / `end`, the bar nodes tied to the host

prestress.title: Prestress
prestress.description: pretensioning: the EFFECTIVE prestress in the bar after losses, Pa, positive in tension. The program computes the elastic-shortening loss (it is what equilibrium at transfer gives) and nothing else -- write sigma_pe here, not sigma_con.

friction.title: Friction
friction.description: post-tensioning friction {mu, k, jack, anchor_set}. With it, `prestress` is the JACKING stress and the solver computes the profile along the tendon; without it, `prestress` is what the whole tendon carries.

unstressed_length.title: Unstressed Length
unstressed_length.description: a `bar` section on a line region as a CABLE: its total unstressed length (an alternative to `prestress`), and whether it carries no compression

unstressed_lengths.title: Unstressed Lengths
unstressed_lengths.description: one per element of the region, in element order (form-finding output)

jack.title: Jack
jack.description: the force (N) a cable is JACKED to: at the end of the analysis step that builds it (the first, when built from the start) each member carries exactly this, whatever the structure gave under it; from then on it is a bar of the unstressed length it ended with. Frame models (beams, bars, connectors) only

tension_only.title: Tension Only
tension_only.description: cable: the member carries no compression (goes slack)

failure.title: Failure
failure.description: elastic-brittle breaking of a line member: see schema.FailureSpec

name.title: Name
name.description: the reinforcement set's name for monitors (`of:`) and result fields; defaults to the section name

ConnectorLawSpec.description:
A path-dependent law on ONE component of a connector:
`gap` (free travel, then a stop), `bilinear` (elastic-plastic with
kinematic hardening: an isolator, a yielding device) or `friction`
(Coulomb: sticks, then slides at mu times the compression another
component of the same connector carries). elements/connector.py has the
mechanics; one scalar of history per component, the slipped deformation.

type.title: Type
type.description: `gap`, `bilinear`, `friction`, `damper` (a fluid viscous damper, F = c sign(v) |v|^alpha; 1.10), `pendulum` (a friction pendulum bearing; 1.10) or `material` (a one-dimensional law of the material table, F = area sigma(d / length); 1.21)

lo.title: Lo
lo.description: gap: lower bound of the free travel (None = no stop that side); friction does not read it (its stick stiffness is `stiffness`)

hi.title: Hi
hi.description: gap: upper bound of the free travel; on the local ux (elongation positive) `{lo: 0}` is a compression-only seat and `{hi: 0}` a tension-only tie

stiffness.title: Stiffness
stiffness.description: gap: the stop's stiffness once a bound is reached; friction, pendulum: the stick stiffness before sliding; damper: a spring beside the damper (optional)

k2.title: K2
k2.description: bilinear: post-yield stiffness (0 = perfectly plastic; must be below k1)

radius.title: Radius
radius.description: pendulum: effective radius of the sliding surface; the restoring stiffness is N / radius, N the compression the bearing carries at that instant

c.title: C
c.description: damper: the coefficient c of F = c sign(v) |v|^alpha (force per velocity^alpha)

exponent.title: Exponent
exponent.description: damper: the velocity exponent alpha, 0 < alpha <= 1 (1 is the linear dashpot; bridges use 0.2-0.5)

linear_below.title: Linear Below
linear_below.description: damper: below this velocity the law is linear, F = c v0^(alpha-1) v; required when alpha < 1 (the power law's slope is infinite at v = 0 and an explicit step chatters there). About 1% of the design velocity

normal.title: Normal
normal.description: friction: where the compression comes from -- `ux` (the current compression of this connector's local ux spring, the one component whose sign does not depend on the node order) or a constant force

material.title: Material
material.description: material: the name of a one-dimensional law in `materials` (parallel, series and gap included)

area.title: Area
area.description: material: force = area x stress; 1 when left out (the table is then the force-deformation relation)

length.title: Length
length.description: material: strain = deformation / length; 1 when left out

ConnectorLawSpec.title: ConnectorLawSpec

region.title: Region
region.description: the nodes the constraint applies to

dofs.title: Dofs
dofs.description: 1 = held/prescribed, 0 = free, in the order [ux, uy, uz, rx, ry, rz]; three entries on a translation-only model

value.title: Value
value.description: prescribed displacement; scalar or 3-vector. None = held at zero.

motion.title: Motion
motion.description: Kinematic quantity prescribed by `value * amplitude(progress)`. Velocity and acceleration are dynamic-analysis conditions.

keep.title: Keep
keep.description: a step's constraint only (1.2): it holds in every later step, until a step's `release` frees its nodes; without it a step's constraint is that step's alone

amplitude.title: Amplitude
amplitude.description: name of an amplitude curve; by default `ramp` (0 to 1 over the step) in a staged relaxation, `ramp_hold` (up to 1, then held) in a continuous relaxation or a dynamic run, and `hold` for a model-level load in a later step and for everything in a time step (`to_age`)

record.description: the support's own ground-motion record (multiple-support excitation): the flagged translational dofs follow it in time

ContactBodySpec.description:
A set of line members that take part in the contact between members,
and the radius of the capsule each of them is (1.11).

region.title: Region
region.description: the region whose members take part (a member is in when both its points are; connectors take no part)

radius.title: Radius
radius.description: the capsule's radius, the distance of the member's surface from its axis. `auto` is for bars and cables alone (the circle of their area); a beam must say

ContactBodySpec.title: ContactBodySpec

rigid.title: Rigid
rigid.description: the rigid surfaces (ground, sea floor, a pile cap ...)

members.description: contact between line members (1.11): a falling span, pounding girders, the pile a collapse leaves

type.title: Type
type.description: NO DEFAULT HERE, DELIBERATELY, AND IT IS THE ONE FIELD THAT NEEDS NONE. The right default depends on the analysis mode -- kinetic for relaxation, undamped for dynamic -- which this file cannot see. It used to default to "kinetic", and because a pydantic model always emits its fields, that made the mode-dependent expression in SIX solvers dead code: every `mode: dynamic` run got kinetic damping, which zeroes the velocity at every kinetic-energy peak and so removes the dynamics it is applied to.  `None` here, resolved in the solver with `or` -- never with a `get` default, which a present-but-None key walks straight past. See `solver_setting` above for the general rule.

coeff.title: Coeff
coeff.description: viscous: damping ratio-like coefficient per unit mass (1/s)

alpha.title: Alpha
alpha.description: Mass-proportional damping, 1/s. Applied under `type: rayleigh`, and ALONGSIDE `type: kinetic` in a relaxation -- refused under `viscous` and `none`, where the frame solvers ignored it. `type: kinetic` with a small alpha is the combination it exists for: kinetic damping only fires when the kinetic energy peaks, so a mode whose energy grows monotonically -- a softening element -- is never touched by it, while alpha*M*v opposes velocity whatever the energy is doing. It is not free: on a softening problem it selects a solution branch (v0.1 has the measurements).

beta.title: Beta
beta.description: stiffness-proportional damping, s; `type: rayleigh` in a dynamic analysis only; makes the stable step smaller

ratio.title: Ratio
ratio.description: Rayleigh stated by its damping ratio at the two `frequencies` (one number, or [zeta_1, zeta_2]); alpha and beta are computed from it

frequencies.title: Frequencies
frequencies.description: the two frequencies (Hz) `ratio` is stated at: usually the first mode and the highest one that matters

regions.title: Regions
regions.description: Rayleigh damping by region (1.22): [{regions: [names], alpha/beta or ratio(/frequencies)}]. The members of the listed regions (with their rigid zones' mass) take this entry's coefficients; the other members and the concentrated masses take the ones above; where two entries overlap the later one holds; an entry's `ratio` without `frequencies` is stated at the two above. `type: rayleigh` in a dynamic run, line models only (core/damping.py)

DiaphragmSpec.description:
A floor that is rigid in its own plane.

The nodes of `region` move together as one rigid body in the plane normal
to `normal`: two translations and the rotation about `normal`. Everything
else -- the out-of-plane translation and the two bending rotations -- stays
free, which is what makes this a diaphragm and not a rigid body.

It is how a building's floor slab is written down when the slab itself is
not meshed, and it is what an OpenSees model means by `rigidDiaphragm`.

normal.title: Normal
normal.description: the plane's normal: the nodes move as a rigid body within the plane normal to it

DiaphragmSpec.title: DiaphragmSpec

ErosionSpec.description:
Element deletion, after Abaqus `ELEMENT DELETION` / LS-DYNA `ERODE`.

A softening model has no answer for a fully degraded element: it still has
nodes and still carries whatever residual force they carry, but no stiffness
to resist it.  Both commercial codes answer by removing the element.

damage.title: Damage
damage.description: damage at or above which the point counts as failed (Abaqus MAX DEGRADATION is 0.99 when elements are kept, 1.0 when they are deleted; MAT_CSCM erodes at d > 0.99)

measure.title: Measure
measure.description: which damage variable `damage` is read from: `d`, the stiffness degradation the stress carries (capped at the material's damage_max, so a threshold above the cap never fires); or `dt` / `dc`, the tensile and compressive variables on their own (CDP's DAMAGET / DAMAGEC, uncapped). `dc` is the spalling rule: crushed concrete goes, cracked concrete stays and keeps holding its bars -- on the Alberta beam a rule on `d` removed the cracked tension zone first.

strain.title: Strain
strain.description: max principal Green-Lagrange strain that must ALSO be exceeded, measured at the element centre. MAT_CSCM spells this as ERODE - 1 and FHWA's own deck uses 0.05. It is a KINEMATIC measure on purpose -- a plastic strain is rescaled by the crack band, so a threshold set for one element size would not carry to another (see continuum.strain_measures).

points.title: Points
points.description: how many of the element's integration points must reach `damage` -- LS-DYNA NUMFIP, whose default of 1 means one failed point out of eight deletes a fully integrated hexahedron. Defaults here to half the points, rounded up.

min_volume_ratio.title: Min Volume Ratio
min_volume_ratio.description: the criterion-free safety net: an element whose volume has collapsed or inverted goes whatever the material says (LS-DYNA *CONTROL_TIMESTEP ERODE with a non-zero DTMIN; Abaqus distortion control exists for this too)

max_volume_ratio.title: Max Volume Ratio
max_volume_ratio.description: an element whose volume has grown by more than this factor is deleted (tangling)

every.title: Every
every.description: iterations between checks -- LS-DYNA checks DR convergence every NRCYCK = 250 cycles for the same reason

ErosionSpec.title: ErosionSpec

FiberShearSpec.description:
A cracking shear law for a fibre section, in series
with the fibres' bending: V = GA0 gamma until the section cracks, then
the cracked stiffness, then (optionally) a stirrup-yield plateau with a
small hardening; unloading and reloading run to the origin once cracked.

The cracked stiffness is given, or taken from the 45-degree truss of the
stirrups (Park & Paulay 1975, sec. 7.3): GA_cr = rho_v / (1 + 4 n rho_v)
E_s b_w d, rho_v = A_v / (b_w s), n = E_s / E_c. The section cracks in
shear when its concrete first cracks in flexure (`cracking: flexural`,
the flexure-shear cracks a frame member actually has), or at a stated
shear force.

direction.title: Direction
direction.description: the direction the shear acts along: `z` (the section's depth, the plane of bending about y) or `y`

cracked_stiffness.title: Cracked Stiffness
cracked_stiffness.description: cracked GA (N); or give `stirrups` for the truss model

web_width.title: Web Width
web_width.description: the web width b_w for the truss model (m); by default the section's width across the shear

cracking.title: Cracking
cracking.description: when it cracks: `flexural` (when the member's concrete first cracks in tension) or a shear force (N)

yield_force.title: Yield Force
yield_force.description: the shear at which the stirrups yield (N); beyond it the stiffness is `hardening` times the cracked one

FiberShearSpec.title: FiberShearSpec

HoopPrim.description:
A closed rectangular tie in the plane normal to `axis`, repeated
along it from `from` to `to` at `spacing`. `corners` are the two
opposite corners in the plane's own two coordinates (the other two
axes in x, y, z order).

corners.title: Corners
corners.description: two opposite corners of the tie in the plane normal to `axis`, in that plane's own two coordinates

axis.title: Axis
axis.description: the axis the ties are stacked along

from.title: From
from.description: coordinate along `axis` of the first tie

divisions.title: Divisions
divisions.description: segments per side of each tie (or `segment_length`)

HoopPrim.title: HoopPrim

HydrodynamicMassSpec.description:
The Morison added mass of members under water:
C_a rho_w A per unit length of the submerged part, across the member and
not along it, weighing nothing. For piers and piles: the members must lie
within 5 degrees of a global axis (a lumped mass is diagonal).

region.title: Region
region.description: the members (both ends in the region)

diameter.title: Diameter
diameter.description: outer diameter of a round section (m); or give `area`

area.title: Area
area.description: the displaced cross-section (m^2), for a section that is not round

coefficient.title: Coefficient
coefficient.description: added-mass coefficient C_a = C_M - 1; 1.0 for a circular cylinder

density.title: Density
density.description: water density: 1025 kg/m^3 by default, converted to the declared `units` when they are not SI (1.025e-9 t/mm^3 in mm/N/s)

water_level.title: Water Level
water_level.description: the free surface: the part of a member below it counts

HydrodynamicMassSpec.title: HydrodynamicMassSpec

LayerPrim.description:
OpenSees `layer straight`: `count` parallel bars from the first at
`from`..`to`, each the next one `spacing` away.

from.title: From
from.description: the first bar, [x, y, z] of its start

spacing.title: Spacing
spacing.description: offset from one bar to the next, [dx, dy, dz]

LayerPrim.title: LayerPrim

LineGroupSpec.description:
One named line of members, straight or an arc, generated (1.1). Its name is
a region: the members' (for `assign`) and their nodes' (for constraints,
loads, monitors), as a Gmsh physical line group's is.

through.title: Through
through.description: the points the line passes through, in order: names from `points` or coordinates [x, y, z]; each pair of neighbours is one segment

size.title: Size
size.description: the target element length: each segment is divided into ceil(length / size)

arc.description: a curve instead of a straight line (two points only): see ArcSpec

LineGroupSpec.title: LineGroupSpec

start.title: Start
start.description: first end of the bar, [x, y, z] in mesh coordinates

divisions.title: Divisions
divisions.description: number of segments along the bar; prefer `segment_length` in a member that cracks (see schema.BarLineSpec)

segment_length.title: Segment Length
segment_length.description: segment length in metres (a physical smearing length for a bonded bar), rounded to whole segments

repeat.title: Repeat
repeat.description: `{count, offset: [dx, dy, dz]}`: `count` copies of the line, each shifted by `offset` from the last

region.title: Region
region.description: the nodes, faces (traction/pressure), volume (body_force/gravity) or members (line_load/moving_load) the load acts on

keep.title: Keep
keep.description: a step's load only (1.2): it stays on in every later step at the value it ended this one with; without it a step's load is that step's alone

vector.title: Vector
vector.description: by default the TOTAL force on the region, spread over its nodes; with per_node it is the force applied at each node instead

moment.title: Moment
moment.description: Total moment (N m): a couple on the nodes of a beam2 model, or on a solid FACE a couple about M's axis with a potential -- in the reference configuration the linear bending traction M z / I (and, for the component along the normal, Saint-Venant's torsion shear) as nodal forces; see core/mesh.FaceMoment.

line_load.title: Line Load
line_load.description: Uniform force per unit member length (N/m), consistently converted to beam end forces and moments. Components are global unless `coordinate_system: local` is selected.

coordinate_system.title: Coordinate System
coordinate_system.description: line_load: `local` gives the components in the member's own axes (x along it)

with_mass.title: With Mass
with_mass.description: line_load: this load is the weight of something (superimposed dead load, surfacing, parapets), so carry its mass |q|/g too, lumped to the members' end nodes in all three translations. The mass weighs nothing (the load IS its weight), so `gravity` does not count it twice; it gives the load inertia in a dynamic run, a modal analysis and a response spectrum. g is 9.80665 m/s² in the declared units. Model-level `loads` only (1.1)

traction.title: Traction
traction.description: constant traction (N/m²) integrated over exterior faces in `region`. Unlike `vector`, this is independent of surface-node density.

pressure.title: Pressure
pressure.description: positive scalar pressure (Pa), acting inward along the exterior normal.

follower.title: Follower
follower.description: pressure: re-integrate it over the faces at their CURRENT positions every step, so it stays normal to the surface it acts on. Face moment: the couple turns with the face and keeps its magnitude through any rotation (the potential -|M| theta of the face's angle about M's axis); without it the reference distribution is a dead load whose couple decays with the cosine of the rotation. The default keeps the reference geometry. Solid elements, numpy/numba.

body_force.title: Body Force
body_force.description: constant force density (N/m³), consistently integrated over volume.

gravity.title: Gravity
gravity.description: acceleration (m/s²); converted to rho * gravity in the selected volume.

temperature.description: A temperature change over the section (see TemperatureSpec).

moving_load.description: Axles travelling along the members of `region` (see MovingLoadSpec).

vehicle.description: a vehicle with mass, suspension and tyres (see VehicleSpec)

ground_motion.title: Ground Motion
ground_motion.description: Uniform base acceleration of the whole model in a dynamic run (frames, fibre beams, trusses, shells, solids): `path` holds two columns (seconds, acceleration), `scale` brings it to the case's acceleration unit (9.80665 for a record in g in an SI case) and `direction` gives the excitation axis. Only these three keys; no amplitude, region `all`.

per_node.title: Per Node
per_node.description: `vector`/`moment` as the force at EACH node rather than the total over the region

amplitude.title: Amplitude
amplitude.description: name in `amplitudes`, or `hold` (full from the first step); by default `ramp` (0 to 1 over the step) in a staged relaxation, `ramp_hold` in a continuous relaxation or a dynamic run, and `hold` for a model-level load in a later step and for a load in a time step (`to_age`)

MassScalingSpec.description:
Selective mass scaling to a target explicit step:
only the DOFs whose own stable step is below `target_dt` get mass, and
exactly as much as lifts them to it. The mass is real -- gravity and a
ground motion see it -- and more than `max_added_fraction` of the model's
translational mass is refused. See vfife/core/mass_scaling.py.

max_added_fraction.title: Max Added Fraction
max_added_fraction.description: refuse when the added translational mass exceeds this fraction of the model's

MassScalingSpec.title: MassScalingSpec

MemberContactSpec.description:
Contact between line members (1.11): each member a
capsule about its axis; two that overlap push each other apart, with a
dashpot and Coulomb friction in a dynamic step. Pairs that overlap in
the reference configuration keep that overlap as an allowance until
they have separated. core/member_contact.py has the mechanics.

bodies.title: Bodies
bodies.description: the bodies, a region and a radius each; every member is tested against every other, its own body's too (not the ones it shares a point with)

stiffness.title: Stiffness
stiffness.description: penalty stiffness: `auto` sizes it from the pair's reduced mass and the step so the step never shrinks for it; a number is capped there

friction.title: Friction
friction.description: Coulomb friction coefficient (acts in dynamic steps only)

damping.title: Damping
damping.description: contact damping ratio zeta (dynamic steps only): an impact loses energy

slack.title: Slack
slack.description: how much closer a pair that overlaps at the start (a girder and the cap under its bearing, neighbours at a joint) may come before the contact acts, as a fraction of the smaller of the two radii (default 5%)

MemberContactSpec.title: MemberContactSpec

type.title: Type
type.description: `box` (dimensions/divisions/origin), `gmsh` (path to .msh), `abaqus` (path to .inp), or `lines`: a line-member mesh written in the case (points/lines, 1.1)

points.title: Points
points.description: lines: named points {name: [x, y, z]}; each name is a region of that one node. No two at one place: a bearing's two sides are two points a little apart, joined by a connector

lines.title: Lines
lines.description: lines: named groups of line members {name: LineGroupSpec}; the name is a region of those members and of their nodes

groups.title: Groups
groups.description: lines: groups of lines {name: [line names]}, an ELEMENT region like a Gmsh physical group of several pieces (for `assign` and `removals`); a `regions:` union is a set of nodes only, and a member whose two nodes are in it belongs to it whichever line it is on. gmsh: groups of the file's physical groups, the same kind of region (the top-level `groups:` lowers to this)

divisions.title: Divisions
divisions.description: box only: elements along x, y, z

origin.title: Origin
origin.description: box only: corner with the smallest x, y, z

path.title: Path
path.description: gmsh only -- path to a .msh, relative to the case file

scale.title: Scale
scale.description: multiplies every coordinate. Meshing in mm and analysing in m is the normal case, and a silent factor of 1000 in the geometry is not the kind of mistake that announces itself.

MonitorSpec.description:
One scalar time history, written to `monitors/<name>` in the result.

Four kinds, and the split is which THING the monitor reduces over:

  reaction, displacement   the NODES of a region
  element                  the ELEMENTS a region owns -- every node of the
                           element inside it, the rule a section
                           assignment already uses
  bar                      the SEGMENTS of one reinforcement set

The last two exist because a verification contract can only read monitors
and whole-model field extrema. Before them, case_15 could not assert the
tendon stress it is built around (bar stress lives in `rebar_steps/`,
which contracts cannot read) and had to stand in the camber for it, and it
could not say "the constant-moment region has not crushed" -- only "no
element anywhere has", which the anchorage zone decides. Both of those
limits are recorded in that case's contract; both are now expressible.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: reaction / displacement (nodes of a region), element (elements of a region), bar (segments of a reinforcement set), fiber (one section point), vehicle (a vehicle named by `of`)

region.title: Region
region.description: the region read (nodal kinds: required; element/bar: narrows to it)

regions.title: Regions
regions.description: nodal kinds: several regions read together

field.title: Field
field.description: element: on solids any per-element output of the material (`dt`, `dc`, `d`, ...) plus `stress` and `von_mises`; on line models any member field (`axial_force`, `bending_y`, `*_max_abs`, `*_i/_j`, `capacity_ratio`, ..., v1.0). bar: `axial_stress`, `axial_force`, `plastic_strain`.

component.title: Component
component.description: which component of a tensor field, in this package's one Voigt order xx, yy, zz, xy, yz, zx (`xz` is read as `zx`)

of.title: Of
of.description: bar: the reinforcement set's name, i.e. the `name` on its assignment

axle.title: Axle
axle.description: vehicle: which axle (contact_force, wheel, station), from 0

reduce.title: Reduce

MovingLoadSpec.description:
A group of axles travelling along the members of a region.

The region's members must form one open chain; `s` is arc length along it
from the end that comes first in (x, y, z), so a bridge laid out along +x
is entered at its left end by a positive `speed`.

`axles` are `[offset, force]` pairs: `offset` is the axle's position along
the path RELATIVE to the group's reference point (so a trailing axle 4.2 m
behind a lead axle is -4.2, whichever way the group travels), and `force`
is its magnitude along `direction`, which defaults to straight down. An
axle whose station is off the path carries nothing, which is how a vehicle
drives on at one end and off at the other.

PathPrim.description:
A bar route through control points, rather than a single straight run.

Two shapes, and the choice between them is not a smoothing preference:

`polyline` (the default) lays a straight leg between each pair of points.
It is exact -- the bar goes where the points say and nowhere else -- and it
is what a bent-up bar, an L-bar, a hook and a HARPED pretensioned tendon
actually are. Each leg is subdivided by `segment_length` (or `divisions`)
the way an ordinary `line` is.

`parabola` takes exactly three points and draws the unique quadratic
through them, with the middle point at the PARAMETER midpoint -- so for the
usual symmetric tendon (anchorage, low point at midspan, anchorage) the
middle point is the low point, and for an asymmetric profile it is not what
you meant and `polyline` is the honest way to say it. The curve is sampled
at EQUAL ARC LENGTH, so `segment_length` means the same physical thing here
as it does on a straight bar (see BarLineSpec: it is a smearing length, not
a discretisation choice), and each chord becomes one bar segment.

A path can `repeat`, exactly as a line can: several parallel tendons or a
row of identical bent-up bars is one entry plus an offset.

WHAT A CURVED TENDON DOES NOT BUY YOU. The geometry is right and the
prestress acts along it -- so the vertical component of a draped tendon
balances load, which is the whole point of draping one. Friction is still
not computed: `prestress` remains the effective stress after losses. What
preflight can now give you is the number a friction calculation needs, the
tendon's total angular change, because a path has one.

shape.title: Shape

in `region` stop carrying load at `time` seconds after the run starts --

Response-spectrum analysis at the state the run ends in:
the modes of the tangent there (as `vfife modal`), each mode's peak from
the spectrum at its period, S_a / omega^2 times its participation, and
the modal peaks combined -- per mode pair by CQC (Der Kiureghian, one

member end actions and support reactions are combined component by

patches.description: `shape: patches`: a fibre section built of quadrilateral patches [{corners: [[y, z] x 4], ny, nz}], each subdivided bilinearly -- a box girder with inclined webs, haunches and tapered cantilevers. Coordinates in the section axes, as `bars`.

shear_stiffness.title: Shear Stiffness
shear_stiffness.description: Effective shear stiffness kappa G A_s [N] of the fibre section. Absent, the member is Euler-Bernoulli; given, the bending interpolation becomes Timoshenko's (Reddy's interdependent element, phi = 12 E I / (GA_s L^2) per member) and a constant shear strain gamma = V / GA_s is added. The fibres do not see shear: this is the elastic (or cracked-effective, e.g. ASCE 41's 0.4 E_c A_w) member shear flexibility, stated by the analyst.

shear.description: a cracking shear law for a fibre section, in series with the bending; exclusive with `shear_stiffness`; in the numba kernel since 1.7

bars.title: Bars
bars.description: [{y, z, section: <bar section name>, count?}] -- OpenSees `layer` per bar; `count` lumps n identical bars at the point

bar_layers.title: Bar Layers
bar_layers.description: bars laid in straight layers (1.2): [{section, from: [y, z], to: [y, z], count | spacing, z_from}] -- both ends included; `spacing` puts as many bars as fit at that spacing or closer (d16 @ 150 over 1 m is 8 bars); `z_from: top | bottom` measures z from that face, downward from the top

tendons.title: Tendons
tendons.description: PRESTRESSING TENDONS of a fibre section: each is {section: <bar section>, profile: [[s, y, z], ...], interpolation: linear | quadratic, normalised: false, prestress: <Pa> | [[s, <Pa>], ...]  |  jack: <Pa>, friction: {mu, k, jack, anchor_set}, elastic_shortening: none | compensate} `profile` is the tendon's line: `s` the distance along the member from its start (the end with the smaller global x, then y, then z; a fraction of the member length when `normalised`), `y`/`z` the offsets in the section axes, as for `bars`; `quadratic` is one parabola through each three consecutive points (0-1-2, 2-3-4, ...: an odd count), and the curve as placed must stay inside the section. The tendon becomes a bonded steel fibre whose position is the profile's value at each element's midpoint -- a draped tendon is a polyline of one eccentricity per element -- carrying an initial strain: `prestress` is the stress the tendon holds with the section unstrained, or `jack` is the stress at the jack and `friction` is the post-tensioning loss profile the embedded tendons already use. What the relaxation then finds is the elastic shortening; `elastic_shortening: compensate` adds the linear-elastic estimate of it back (the gross section's 3x3 stiffness about the origin, so a T or a box need not be written about its centroid), so the stated stress is what the tendon carries against the hardened, already-shortened concrete.

fracture.title: Fracture
fracture.description: `fracture: {threshold: 1.0}` -- the member is severed when that fraction of its fibres has failed. On the SECTION and not on the assignment because it is the section that says how many fibres there are and which laws they carry; what makes a fibre fail is in the material block.

TemperatureSpec.description:
A temperature change over a member's section.

Temperature is not a force. It is a FREE STRAIN the section would take on
if nothing held it: eps_th(y, z) = alpha * T(y, z). What that produces
depends entirely on what is in the way --

  * nothing in the way (a determinate member, a linear T): the member
    simply changes shape. It elongates by alpha dT L, it bows to a
    curvature alpha dT/dy, and it carries NO stress at all.
  * something in the way (a restrained end, a redundant support): the part
    of the free strain the structure refuses becomes force -- an axial
    N = EA alpha dT, a continuous beam's secondary moments.
  * a NONLINEAR T through the depth (which is what a bridge code's design
    profile is): even a simply supported beam cannot take that shape,
    because plane sections must stay plane. The section keeps the linear
    part as elongation and curvature and turns the rest into
    self-equilibrated stresses -- zero net force, zero net moment, and
    real stress. Only a fibre section can show them: a `profile` on a
    `beam2` / `beam2_timoshenko` section (shaped or `general`) is refused,
    not reduced -- reducing it needs the area distribution a beam section
    does not carry.

The field is `uniform` + `gradient`, or a `profile` sampled through the
section. `gradient` is K per metre of section depth rather than "top minus
bottom", because a `general` beam section states area and second moments
and has no depth to divide by.

uniform.title: Uniform
uniform.description: K, the whole section (positive = warmer than the stress-free state)

gradient.title: Gradient
gradient.description: [dT/dy, dT/dz] in K/m along the section's own axes; a scalar is the gradient along `axis` (y by default: [g, 0]; `axis: z` gives [0, g]).

profile.title: Profile
profile.description: [[s, T], ...] through the section (m, K), linear between the points and constant beyond the ends -- a code's design profile written literally. Mutually exclusive with uniform/gradient.

axis.title: Axis
axis.description: which of the section's own axes the profile, or a scalar gradient, runs along. A `rect`/`box` has its depth on z (width along y); a `patches` section on whichever axis its corners put it -- so a deck's vertical profile names the axis rather than assuming one. Refused with a two-component gradient, which names its axes already.

FractureSpec.description:
When an element stops carrying load, and what happens then.

ONE NUMBER, because everything else about fracture is decided elsewhere on
purpose (core/fracture.py): WHEN a material point is finished is the
material's business and is written in the material block (a bar's
`rupture_strain`, a damage law's own limit), and HOW the points of this
element family add up is the element's and is not a choice at all. What is
left for the analyst is how much of the section has to be gone before the
member is treated as severed, and the honest default is all of it.

threshold.title: Threshold
threshold.description: fraction of the section's fibres (or a solid's Gauss points) that must have failed. 1.0 = the whole section; lower cuts the member earlier, which is a modelling shortcut and should be said out loud in a report.

split.title: Split
split.description: separate the member from the frame when it fractures, instead of only switching its forces off. The member's share of the mass moves onto particles of its own and the fragment falls. Off by default because it is a different analysis: it needs solver.mode = dynamic, it reserves two particles per element, and what the debris then lands on is not modelled yet -- there is no contact.

FractureSpec.title: FractureSpec

BondSpec.description:
Bond stress-slip between an embedded bar and its host.

Present means the bar gets its OWN degrees of freedom and may slip; absent
means perfect bond, which is cheaper, runs on every backend, and is right
whenever the member is not expected to crack. See materials/bond.py for the
law and v0.1 for why the choice matters more than it looks.

TWO LAWS SHIP, AND THE DEFAULT IS THE MONOTONIC ONE
    `bond_ceb`     the MC2010 envelope with a linear unloading rule. Right
                   for a pushover; under a long cyclic history it
                   overstates the bond that survives, which is the unsafe
                   direction.
    `bond_cyclic`  the same envelope with Eligehausen-type degradation and
                   a pinched reversal. Identical to `bond_ceb` on a
                   monotonic path, bit for bit, so switching costs nothing
                   but the extra state.

    The default stays `bond_ceb` because changing it would silently
    re-rate every model that already names a bond block.

type.title: Type
type.description: the bond-slip law: `bond_ceb` (MC2010 monotonic) or `bond_cyclic`; every other key is that material's parameter

TendonFrictionSpec.description:
Post-tensioning friction: sigma(s) = sigma_con exp(-(mu theta + k s)).

With this present, `prestress` is sigma_con AT THE JACK and the solver
derives the stress in every segment; without it, `prestress` is the value
the whole tendon carries. That is the one place the meaning of a field
depends on another, and preflight says which reading is in force.

k.description: wobble coefficient, per metre of tendon

jack.description: which end the jack is at; `both` takes the smaller loss at each point

FailureSpec.description:
When a line member breaks: ELASTIC-BRITTLE -- linear
until the criterion, then gone. Dynamic runs only; per member group in a
mixed_line model (`assign[].failure`), for every member of a single-
section beam2/beam2_timoshenko/truss2 model (`element.failure`).

A bar (cable) breaks when its tension reaches `tensile_strength` x area.
A beam breaks when, at either end, |N|/(A f_y) + |M_y|/M_y,cap +
|M_z|/M_z,cap >= 1 with M_cap = shape_factor f_y I / c: `extreme_fibre`
is [c_y, c_z], the distances from the member axis to the extreme fibres
along the section's local y and z. Shear and torsion are not checked
against a strength; but a beam twisted a quarter turn end to end is
removed (the co-rotational frame cannot follow half a turn), and a
piece broken at both ends is removed once its demand reaches twice its
capacity (it is still steel).

Why not a strain limit: in an elastic member the strain at which steel
actually tears (15%) is reached only at 30 000 MPa, so the member would
never break first; a CAPACITY is what an elastic member can be checked
against, and it needs only A, I and the depth of the section.

tensile_strength.title: Tensile Strength
tensile_strength.description: bars and cables: the tension at which the member breaks, Pa

yield_strength.title: Yield Strength
yield_strength.description: beams: the yield strength (Pa) behind N_p = f_y A and M_cap = shape_factor f_y I / c

extreme_fibre.title: Extreme Fibre
extreme_fibre.description: beams: [c_y, c_z], the distances (m) from the member axis to the extreme fibres along the section's local y and z

shape_factor.title: Shape Factor
shape_factor.description: plastic over elastic moment (1 = first yield; a thin-walled box about 1.12)

rotation_capacity.title: Rotation Capacity
rotation_capacity.description: beams (mixed_line): given, every end is a PLASTIC HINGE -- the end moments are capped on |N|/N_p + |M_y|/M_y,p + |M_z|/M_z,p <= 1, what would exceed it becomes plastic rotation, and the end breaks when its accumulated plastic rotation (rad) reaches this; left out, elastic-brittle: the end breaks the moment the capacity is reached

split.title: Split
split.description: after the break: true splits the member off onto its own particles with its mass (a free elastic segment), false only deactivates it (mass stays on the nodes); left out, frames and mixed_line split, the standalone truss deactivates
